stem: During a transfer request, before dispensing Xyrem, a pharmacist reviews both controlled-substance and product-specific obligations. Select all supported conclusions.

choices.text: On this record, current product-specific REMS requirements must be satisfied for sodium oxybate.
For this scenario, federal Schedule III refill limits remain independently applicable for sodium oxybate.
Under these facts, xyrem is Schedule III when it is an FDA-approved sodium oxybate product under the federal scheduling exception.
In this setting, rEMS compliance does not displace ordinary controlled-substance record duties for sodium oxybate.
At this stage, rEMS enrollment converts the drug to Schedule VI for sodium oxybate.

related_facts: sodium oxybate (Xyrem) is used for treatment of cataplexy or excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy; it is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III.
A pharmacy dispensing a drug subject to an FDA REMS must follow the current product-specific certification, authorization, documentation, and safe-use requirements that apply to the dispenser.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
